# 1 Clement Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_001_page_001.jpg

---

## Salutation

**1:Salutation** The Church of God which sojourns in Rome to the Church of God which sojourns in Corinth — to those who are called and sanctified by the will of God through our Lord Jesus Christ: Grace and peace be multiplied to you from God Almighty through Jesus Christ.

---

## Chapter 1

**1:1** On account of the sudden and successive calamities and reverses that have come upon us, brothers, we acknowledge that we have been somewhat tardy in giving attention to the matters of contention among you, beloved — even to that detestable and unholy sedition, so utterly foreign and alien to the elect of God, which a few rash and self-willed persons have fanned into such a pitch of frenzy that your honorable and celebrated name — so worthy of universal love — has been grievously reproached.

**1:2** For who among those who had stayed with you did not prove your most excellent and steadfast faith? Who did not admire your prudent and moderate godliness in Christ? Who did not proclaim the splendor of your practice of hospitality? Who did not pronounce blessed your complete and certain knowledge?

**1:3** For you conducted all things without favoritism, and you walked in the ordinances of God, submitting yourselves to your leaders, and giving fitting honor to those older among you. Upon the young you enjoined thoughts that are moderate and seemly. The women you directed to carry out all things in a blameless, reverent, and pure conscience, rendering due affection to their own husbands; and you taught them to remain in the rule of submission and to manage their households decorously and with every fitting discretion.

---

*LOGOS renders according to standard Greek text of Codex Alexandrinus with attention to formal correspondence.*
